x: A "veteran" of two Cup Finals and two seasons of dominating the Women's Southern League sprint events, it's a sobering thought that seventeen year-old sprint star Amala Onuora is only just entering the under 20 age group in 2003.
In the European Youth Olympic Festival, we were represented by Wade Bennett-Jackson, who took gold in both the 100 m and 200 m, Amala Onuora and Chris Gearing.

A highly motivated (when is she anything but?) Amala Onuora prepared for her trip to Paris for the 'Youth Olympics' the following weekend by clocking 12.0 seconds in the 100m and she later anchored the winning 4 x 100m relay team.
Amala Onuora made a good start to her season with a 12.2 win in the 100m and 25.5 for 2nd in the 200m. She also ran the anchor leg in the sprint relay and made a bold bid to snatch second place.

Below: Rachel King, Amala Onuora, Michelle Nestor and Caroline Wilson joined forces to win the 4 x 100m relay at the Golden Jubilee Cup Semi-Final and help push the score along to a massive 313 out of a maximum possible of 342.

And while Wade was grabbing the headlines, let's not forget two great runs from Amala Onuora - a fine supporter of our women's teams as she reached the semi-final stage of the women's 200 metres and ran second stage in the sprint relay.
